howWeSearched.scope: Published texts on six propositions about AI and biology (P1 to P6): papers and their abstracts, perspectives, journal news articles, company announcements and press releases. Developer model papers are the subject of the `models` pass and company statements of the `companies` pass; this pass records only their stance on a proposition. Biosecurity propositions are left to the ai-bio-pack.
routes: Europe PMC REST search (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/search?query=…&format=json), lite results sorted by publication date ascending, then core records (resultType=core) for abstracts and dates; Europe PMC full-text XML (/PMC…/fullTextXML) where open
Article pages on nature.com (Nature, Nature Methods, Nature Medicine, Nature Reviews Drug Discovery, Scientific Reports), retrieved directly
arXiv abstract pages (arxiv.org/abs/…v1) and the bioRxiv details API (api.biorxiv.org/details/biorxiv/<doi>)
Company sites retrieved directly: deepmind.google, isomorphiclabs.com (news listing and articles), evolutionaryscale.ai, sumitomo-pharma.com, insilico.com (news listing, to locate release addresses)
Internet Archive availability API for one capture (deepmind.com, December 2020)

Candidate lookup by title or DOI: several texts (Wong et al. 2022, Terwilliger et al. 2023, Lyu et al. 2024, Ma et al. 2018, Ahlmann-Eltze et al. 2025, Jayatunga et al. 2024, Xu et al. 2025, Huang et al. 2016, Anishchenko et al. 2020/2021, Watson et al. 2023, Bunne et al. 2024) were looked up as candidates by title or DOI rather than found by the term searches below; every record rests on the text then retrieved. Such lookups find what is already known and bias the earliest-located roles toward well-cited texts.

termsAndYears.P1: Europe PMC: TITLE_ABS "structure prediction" AND "drug design", 1970–1995 (3 hits); ABSTRACT "structure prediction" AND drug, 1970–1994 (2 hits); TITLE "prediction of protein structures", 1970–1990 (2 hits); abstract phrases "predicted structure", "structure prediction", "predicting the structure", "tertiary structure" with "drug design" or "design of drugs", 1960–1987 (0 hits, which shows phrase matching is exact and that Blundell et al. 1987 was found only through the title search); TITLE AlphaFold AND "drug discovery", 2020–2023 (6 hits). DeepMind's 2020 account was read because the dataset already holds it.
termsAndYears.P2: Europe PMC: TITLE_ABS "virtual cell", 1960–2001 (18 hits; the earliest is a 1993 Trends in Genetics title by Casini with no abstract, not read); "virtual cell" with machine learning, deep learning, artificial intelligence or neural network, to 2021 (2 hits, neither on the criterion); "virtual cell", "whole-cell model", "model of a cell" or "simulate cell" with deep learning, neural network or artificial intelligence, MEDLINE, 1990–2023 (43 hits, none earlier than Ma et al. 2018 on the criterion); TITLE "virtual cell challenge" (3 hits). The combined search did not return Ma et al. 2018, which was looked up by its title as a candidate and then retrieved; searches for "in silico cell" and "cell simulation" with machine learning were not run, so the P2 earliest-located role is weakly bounded.
termsAndYears.P3: No bibliographic search was run for company statements: the Sumitomo Dainippon Pharma and Exscientia release of January 2020 and Insilico Medicine's statements were located from the companies' own newsrooms. Earlier company statements that a named AI-discovered candidate began a trial (for example from companies founded before 2015) were not searched; press-release archives (Business Wire, PR Newswire, GlobeNewswire) were not searched systematically, and GlobeNewswire refused the one release tried.
termsAndYears.P4: Europe PMC: TITLE_ABS "protein design" with neural network, machine learning, deep learning or artificial intelligence, to 2018 (39 hits, mostly stability prediction and engineering of natural proteins, none meeting the criterion); TITLE "protein design" with deep, neural, machine learning or generative, 2015–2020 (9 hits). The earliest located (Anishchenko et al., bioRxiv v1 of 23 July 2020) is bounded: preprints on generative models for protein design from 2019 (gcWGAN, autoregressive generative models; Europe PMC preprint records) were listed but not read, and could meet the criterion.
termsAndYears.P5: Europe PMC: abstract phrases "biology is an informational science", "biology has become an information science", "biology is an information science" (12 hits; Hood and Galas 2003 read). No search was run for "programmable biology", "digital biology" or "language of life" with machine learning, and no book or lecture literature was searched; the earliest located (Isomorphic Labs, 2021) is weakly bounded.
termsAndYears.P6: Located through the companies and trial texts above (Jayatunga et al. 2024 by title search in Europe PMC). No systematic search for analyses of AI-discovered drug success rates was run; later analyses (2025–2026) may exist.

gaps: Paywalled article bodies were not read: Nature (1987, 2003, 2016), Nature Methods (2018) and the Nature and Nature Reviews Drug Discovery news articles were read in their abstracts or standfirsts only. Five texts (Sternberg 1992, Tomita 2001, Lyu 2024, Jayatunga 2024, Roohani 2025) were read only in Europe PMC records of their abstracts.

science.org was not tried (refused per the brief); the PMC page for Lyu et al. returned a browser check and the Europe PMC full text returned HTTP 500; the Elsevier page for Jayatunga et al. returned no readable text; cell.com was not tried.

Europe PMC abstract coverage before the mid-1970s is thin, so P1 and P2 searches cannot show earlier texts; no book, conference proceedings (for example ISMB, Pacific Symposium on Biocomputing) or pre-1987 review literature was searched.
No non-English text was searched; Chinese-language texts on these propositions (for example from BioMap or XtalPi) were not looked for.
Interviews, talks, op-eds and general press were not searched; DeepMind's and Isomorphic Labs' other posts were listed but only the two recorded were read.

The pages of DeepMind (2020), Isomorphic Labs (2021) and EvolutionaryScale (2024) were read as served on 2026-10-30; their wording is attested from that date. The December 2020 Internet Archive capture of DeepMind's account returned HTTP 403.

howWeSearched.note: "Earliest located" means the earliest text these searches found that meets the proposition's criterion and that was retrieved and checked here. It is not a claim that no earlier text exists, and it says nothing about influence between the texts. Searches ran on 2026-10-30.

claims.subject: aib-doc-blundell-1987
claims.statement: The Nature review "Knowledge-based prediction of protein structures and the design of novel molecules" (Blundell, Sibanda, Sternberg and Thornton, 26 March 1987) states that knowledge-based prediction techniques are of value in predicting receptor structures to aid the design of drugs.

time.note: Publication and issue date printed on the Nature article page.

claims.qualification: The record documents what this text states, in its register; it is not evidence that the proposition is true and implies no influence on or from any other text. The method the abstract describes is knowledge-based modelling from analogies with known structures, not machine learning; the record bears on the AI period only as an earlier statement of the same expectation. Only the abstract was read. Earliest located for this proposition among the texts found by the searches in howWeSearched; not a claim that no earlier text exists.

thought.qualifier: Stated of knowledge-based (comparative) modelling, as a field of use; no drug is named.

evidence.passage: Such techniques are of value in prediction of receptor structures to aid the design of drugs, herbicides or pesticides, antigens in vaccine design, and novel molecules in protein engineering.
evidence.note: The text is the primary source for its own statement.

evidence.locator: Abstract (article page), what the techniques are
evidence.passage: Prediction of the tertiary structures of proteins may be carried out using a knowledge-based approach.
evidence.note: Shows that the predicted structures in question are computational predictions, not experimental structures.

claims.subject: aib-doc-sternberg-1992
claims.statement: The Faraday Discussions paper "Modelling the structure and function of enzymes by machine learning" (Sternberg, Lewis, King and Muggleton, 1992) reports applying the machine-learning program GOLEM both to protein secondary-structure prediction and, separately, to modelling a structure-activity relationship in drug design.

time.note: Year of the Faraday Discussions issue (vol. 93) as given by Europe PMC; no finer date was retrieved.

claims.qualification: The record documents what this text states, in its register; it is not evidence that the proposition is true and implies no influence on or from any other text. Read in the Europe PMC record of the abstract only. Kept as context because it is the earliest located text in these searches that joins machine learning, protein structure prediction and drug design in one study.

thought.missing: Does not state that predicted protein structures aid drug design: the structure-prediction and drug-design applications are separate, and the drug-design model rests on ligand activities, not on a predicted protein structure.

evidence.passage: the prediction of protein secondary structure from sequence and (2) modelling a quantitative structure-activity relationship in drug design.
evidence.note: Abstract text relayed by Europe PMC's record of the PubMed abstract: the authors' own text, so primary; the journal expression was not read. The two applications are listed as separate problems.

claims.subject: alphafold-account
claims.statement: DeepMind's account of AlphaFold at CASP14 (dated 30 November 2020) states that insights from protein structure predictions could enable more precise work on drug development, complementing existing experimental methods.

time.note: Date printed on the page. The wording is attested only in the copy served on 2026-10-30, which carries a July 2022 update notice at its head; the December 2020 Internet Archive capture could not be opened (HTTP 403).

claims.qualification: The record documents what this text states, in its register; it is not evidence that the proposition is true and implies no influence on or from any other text. Stated as a possibility ("could"), of insights from work with a small number of specialist groups. A developer's statement about its own system. The page also quotes third parties on drug discovery; those relays are not recorded here.

thought.qualifier: A possibility, framed as complementing experimental methods.

evidence.locator: Section on next steps, paragraph beginning "In the meantime"
evidence.passage: These insights could enable more precise work on drug development, complementing existing experimental methods to find promising treatments faster.
evidence.note: The developer is the primary source for its own statement.

evidence.passage: we're also looking into how protein structure predictions could contribute to our understanding of specific diseases with a small number of specialist groups
evidence.note: Shows that "these insights" are insights from protein structure predictions.

claims.subject: aib-doc-mullard-2021
claims.statement: Mullard's Nature Reviews Drug Discovery news article "What does AlphaFold mean for drug discovery?" (14 September 2021) says in its standfirst that the implications of AlphaFold and RoseTTAFold for drug discovery are more incremental than their advance in structure prediction.

time.note: Date printed on the article page.

claims.qualification: The record documents what this text states, in its register; it is not evidence that the proposition is true and implies no influence on or from any other text. Journalism (secondary source). Only the standfirst and the opening paragraph were readable; the body, which may give the reasoning and named sources, was not read.

openQuestions.question: P1's criterion is not limited to AI, so its earliest located text (Blundell et al. 1987) is knowledge-based modelling. Keep the criterion broad, or narrow it to machine-learning predictions?
openQuestions.recommended: Keep it broad: the expectation that predicted structures aid drug design predates machine-learning structure prediction, which is what the record shows; the qualification says the 1987 method is not machine learning.

openQuestions.question: Should records resting only on a Europe PMC abstract record (five texts) be admitted, or held until the article itself is read?
openQuestions.recommended: Admit as abstract-level records with the source labelled as the Europe PMC record, and reread at the publisher where access allows; the earliest-located role for P6 (Jayatunga et al.) should be rechecked against the article before admission.

openQuestions.question: Ahlmann-Eltze et al. (2025) are recorded as contesting P2 (present-tense half only). Is "contests" right, or should it be context?
openQuestions.recommended: Contests, with the qualifier as written: the paper disputes, for the tested models, the capability the criterion states in its present tense; the cross-family check should look at this record.

openQuestions.question: The pages of Isomorphic Labs (2021) and EvolutionaryScale (2024) name or omit authors differently from the labs pass's possible records of the same pages. Who owns these documents?
openQuestions.recommended: The labs pass, if it defines them; the integrator should merge the document ids (aib-doc-isomorphic-intro-2021, aib-doc-evolutionaryscale-esm3-post-2024) into its ids.
